blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, audit and internal controls are not an administrative function — they are a leadership discipline that protects the company, the team, and the honest people who work inside it. A controls culture that is genuinely alive catches mistakes before they become disasters, provides early warning of deeper problems, and gives senior leaders the confidence to act decisively because they trust the numbers in front of them.

The temptation, at the top, is to treat controls as cost — something to be thinned in good times and rebuilt hastily in bad ones. This is almost always a false economy. The value of controls appears not on a quiet Tuesday, but on the one morning when something has gone wrong and somebody asks, how did we let that happen? A company with living controls has an answer. A company without them has a panic.

Senior finance leaders protect audit and controls as they protect any other strategic capability — funded properly, reviewed regularly, respected publicly. The companies that do this rarely appear in the news for the wrong reasons. That quiet absence, across years, is the real signature of good executive finance leadership.

items.q: According to the text, how should audit and internal controls be understood at executive level?
options: As a cost to be thinned in good times
As a public-relations exercise
As a leadership discipline that protects the company
As an administrative function
items.why: "they are a leadership discipline that protects the company, the team, and the honest people" — o texto rejeita a leitura de que seja mero função administrativa.

items.q: What does the text say a living controls culture provides?
options: Lower audit fees and faster reporting
A guarantee that no mistake will ever occur
Early warning of deeper problems and the confidence to act decisively
A way to reduce headcount in the finance team
items.why: "provides early warning of deeper problems, and gives senior leaders the confidence to act decisively".

items.q: Why does the author call thinning controls in good times a "false economy"?
options: Because good times never actually last very long
Because rebuilding them costs slightly more than maintaining them
Because auditors charge a premium during downturns
Because their value shows up precisely when something goes wrong
items.why: "The value of controls appears not on a quiet Tuesday, but on the one morning when something has gone wrong" — cortar parece poupar, mas custa caro quando o problema chega.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Good controls rarely announce themselves in headlines.
Controls deserve steady funding even when nothing seems to be wrong.
In lean periods, controls are the sensible place to make quick savings.
A company without living controls is exposed on the day something fails.
items.why: Inferência: o texto trata o corte de controles em tempos bons como falsa economia, então discordaria da ideia de que são o lugar sensato para economizar.

items.q: What does "that quiet absence, across years" suggest about strong finance leadership?
options: That its success is measured by scandals and crises that never happen
That the best leadership avoids public communication entirely
That controls make no measurable difference to a business
That finance teams should stay out of the press for legal reasons
items.why: Inferência: "rarely appear in the news for the wrong reasons" — a boa liderança se prova pela ausência de desastres, algo que não gera manchete.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte encerrar o programa de reconstrução da cultura de controles. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Two years ago, when we started this, controls in this company were tolerated, not respected. They were the box you ticked before the real work began. Today I want to mark the end of that programme — and, more importantly, the end of that attitude.

Let me be candid about why this mattered. When I arrived, we had thinned our controls quietly, year after year, because the business was doing well and nobody missed them. That is exactly how these things fail. The bill never arrives on a good day. It arrives on the morning something has gone wrong and a board member asks how we let it happen — and you either have an answer or you have a very long silence.

So we funded this properly, we reviewed it every quarter, and we talked about it in public, on purpose. Not because controls are glamorous — they are not — but because what you protect openly, people take seriously.

Here is the part I want you to remember. If we have done our job, you will not read about this company for the wrong reasons. Not this year, not in five years. That silence is not nothing. That silence is the work.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Charlotte describe the status of controls when the programme began?
options: Tolerated, not respected — a box to be ticked
Recently rebuilt after a crisis
Managed entirely by external auditors
Respected and generously funded
items.why: "controls in this company were tolerated, not respected. They were the box you ticked."

items.q: According to Charlotte, why had controls been thinned before she arrived?
options: Because regulators had relaxed the requirements
Because the finance team was too small to run them
Because the business was doing well and nobody missed them
Because a previous crisis had discredited them
items.why: "we had thinned our controls quietly, year after year, because the business was doing well and nobody missed them."

items.q: What are the three things Charlotte says she did to protect the programme?
options: Centralised it, simplified it, and kept it confidential
Hired consultants, cut costs, and rebranded the team
Outsourced it, automated it, and reported it annually
Funded it properly, reviewed it quarterly, and talked about it in public
items.why: "we funded this properly, we reviewed it every quarter, and we talked about it in public, on purpose."

items.q: What does Charlotte imply by "what you protect openly, people take seriously"?
options: Public visibility signals importance and shapes behaviour
Only glamorous work deserves public attention
Employees resent being watched too closely
Confidential programmes always fail
items.why: Inferência: falar do tema em público não é vaidade — é o que faz a equipe levá-lo a sério.

items.q: When Charlotte says "that silence is the work," she most likely means that success will be measured by…
options: the awards the finance team receives
how little the team communicates internally
the crises and headlines that never occur
the number of audits completed each year
items.why: Inferência: o resultado do trabalho é não aparecer no noticiário pelos motivos errados — a ausência de desastre é a prova.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She refused to treat compliance as a mere administrative function." An administrative function is…
options: a source of competitive advantage
a routine, procedural task run for its own sake
a board-level governance committee
a strategic bet on future growth
items.why: Administrative function = função administrativa: tarefa rotineira e procedimental, o oposto de disciplina de liderança.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The dashboard flagged the anomaly weeks early, giving the board an ___ of the liquidity squeeze."
options: false economy
absence
administrative function
early warning
items.why: Early warning = aviso prévio: o sinal antecipado de um problema mais profundo.

items.q: "Cutting the internal audit team looked prudent, but it proved a false economy." A false economy is…
options: a deliberate off-book transaction
a saving that ends up costing more than it saved
an accounting error in the ledger
a downturn caused by weak demand
items.why: False economy = falsa economia: parece poupar, mas sai mais caro depois.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "With numbers she could trust, she was able to act ___ instead of hedging every decision."
options: hastily
decisively
reluctantly
administratively
items.why: Decisively = decisivamente: agir com firmeza, exatamente o que os controles confiáveis permitem.

items.q: "A living controls culture catches errors before they become disasters." This phrase refers to…
options: the regulatory calendar of filing deadlines
a shared, active way of working in which controls are respected and used
the external auditor's annual opinion
the physical archive of audit documents
items.why: Controls culture = cultura de controles: o hábito coletivo e vivo de respeitar e usar os controles.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e auditoria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The audit committee still has to sign off on the revised controls framework." To sign off on means to…
options: quietly shelve
audit line by line
circulate for comment
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new control checks region by region over two quarters." To roll out means to…
options: present to the board
implement in stages
abandon in phases
test in secret
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Trimming the audit budget in a strong year is a false economy that comes back to bite you." This means it will…
options: improve results in the short term only
go unnoticed by the board
be reversed automatically by regulators
cause harm later that outweighs the early saving
items.why: Come back to bite you = voltar para te prejudicar; combina com a ideia de falsa economia da lição.

items.q: "The team designed the framework but never followed through on the quarterly reviews." They…
options: changed it every quarter
delegated it to the auditors
failed to carry the commitment to completion
documented it too thoroughly
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, as revisões que ficaram por fazer.

items.q: "A single dashboard tweak will not move the needle on our controls culture." This means it will…
options: take years to install
alarm the regulators
breach a reporting standard
not make a noticeable difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
